provenMechanisms: A canonical Wiki assertion is deterministically supported by one active canonical Claim and resolvable evidence.
A SUPERSEDES-driven transaction found and rebuilt 3/3 affected Wiki modules while preserving stable addresses.
Old Claim references were removed, replacement references were present, old Wiki copies were quarantined, and 3/3 unrelated modules remained byte-stable.
Failure injected after Wiki publication restored canonical Wiki, quarantine and knowledgeVersion.
Materialized Wiki consumption was a real treatment: W packs contained supported Wiki modules while paired R0 packs disabled them.
The final post-hoc answer run had 12/12 valid formats and citation closure after one bounded citation-repair call; affected old-error recurrence and unrelated hard regression were both zero.
notProven: M1 does not prove that a one-assertion Wiki improves average answer quality over R0.
M1 does not prove automatic Wiki formation, multi-source synthesis, best module granularity, or held-out generalization.

The model judge is not authoritative: its first contract inferred explicit threshold and vulnerability facts from the broad phrase 'tests passed'; the strict contract still assigned identical fact rationales to two materially different answers.

manualAudit.rootCause: The affected Wiki fixture intentionally materialized only the superseded assertion. It proved correction lifecycle, but it was not a complete stable-question knowledge module; R0 retrieval also omitted several active claims required for a complete answer.

excludes: provider-side work from transport failures when no usage record was returned

nextMilestone.name: 完整问题模块与增量纠错
nextMilestone.primaryQuestion: Can a multi-assertion, evidence-closed Wiki module preserve a complete answer bundle across updates, improve required-fact coverage over the same R0 base, and do so within a fixed visible-token budget?
nextMilestone.requiredMechanism: Build or curate a complete module around a stable question using multiple single-Claim assertions; update only affected assertions while unrelated assertions and stableAddress remain unchanged.
nextMilestone.stopRule: Do not request a new held-out set until M2 passes on development episodes without domain-specific branches.
